The project's own Rust, PHP, R and Python code and original documentation use the
**MIT license**, copyright 2026 Erik Westlund. The exact text is in the repository's
root LICENSE; both Rust crate manifests declare the SPDX identifier `MIT`.

This does not relicense third-party material:

- Bundled published datasets retain their original provenance and licenses. See
  [Gaussian mixed-model data](data/lmm/index.qmd),
  [the preserved package license](data/lmm/COPYING),
  [dataset provenance](data/lmm/sources.json), and
  [cbpp provenance](data/cbpp-source.json).
- Rust dependencies retain the licenses declared in their own packages.
  The explicit sampling dependencies `rand 0.9.5` and `rand_chacha 0.9.0` use the
  MIT option of their dual licenses; notices and source hashes are retained under
  `third-party/` and `third-party/sources.json`.
- Vendored Quarto web assets retain their embedded third-party notices.
- R, ggplot2 and other development tools retain their own licenses; they are not
  runtime dependencies of the PHP extension.

The MIT choice covers project-owned files; preserve applicable third-party notices
when redistributing the library, documentation or data.
